text:
maria: heads-up — I profiled a live canary and saw host-side parse + slice work jump from ~3.1ms to 9.2ms for streaming requests after the latest routing change.
ajay: ouch. which routing change? the kernel selection fallback?
maria: not the kernel. it's the new 'parse-slicer' middleware we added to normalize incoming chunks before KV cache lookup. seems to re-tokenize prefixes for every chunk.
ajay: re-tokenize for every chunk sounds bad. we intended incremental tokenization keyed by connection. can you paste the hot path?
maria: here's the simplified trace I captured:```\nParseSlicer.processChunk() -> normalizeUtf8() -> incrementalTokenize() -> sliceToFrame() -> kvCache.lookup(prefixKey)\nBut incrementalTokenize is doing a new token scan because slice boundaries are recomputed every time (we call normalizeUtf8 on the whole buffer).\n```\najay: @maria can you add the actual memcpy/alloc numbers? is this CPU-bound or alloc-bound?
maria: CPU-bound mainly. Flame shows ~70% of the extra time in UTF normalizer + decode loop. allocs per request went up too (small buffers) but GC not the main offender.
eva: the batching heuristics might be feeding us tiny chunks intentionally (low-latency streaming). if we coalesce on host we'll increase tail latency for some flows. need a careful fix.
dmitri: two ideas: (1) make normalizeUtf8 incremental — only feed new bytes, keep decoder state per connection. (2) change the path to do KV cache lookup using raw bytes + stable fingerprint, then tokenize only on cache miss.
kevin: (2) is appealing — cheap fingerprinting (xxhash64) on raw bytes then consult kv. avoids repeated tokenization for cached prefixes. but need to prove collision footguns are negligible.
ajay: any perf regression on gRPC vs HTTP? our regression tests showed larger delta on gRPC streams.
maria: yes, gRPC had ~12ms delta vs ~6ms on HTTP/1.1 for identical payloads. turns out our gRPC framing layer does small-slice reads (200-800b) while HTTP/2 is batching better in the client lib.
eva: maybe we should introduce a host-side coalescer per call that merges small incoming slices up to X ms or Y bytes, but only for non-blocking streaming paths. config knob.
dmitri: caution: coalescer interacts with our latency SLOs. propose: default coalescing=disabled; enable for dedicated pools as an opt-in perf optimization.
kevin: one more angle — kernel selection: some model kernels prefer longer contiguous tokens for attention perf. if host-side slicing fragments sequences, we hurt GPU throughput later (short seq kernels spin up more). worth measuring token sequence continuity post-slicing.
ajay: good point. add a metric: "sequence_fragmentation_ratio" (num-contiguous-prefixes / tokens) in tracing.
maria: I'll prototype two patches tonight: incremental normalizer state + xxhash prefix fingerprinting. will run e2e microbench.
opsbot: deploy: canary/parse-slicer-fix started by maria at 2026-03-18T02:21:00Z :rocket:
kevin: ping when you have flame graphs — I'll compare against the kernel-selection perf numbers.
maria: thanks — will post results here. :thumbsup:
